title: Fragment-level indexing and deduplication for prompt cache (GPU-resident canonical store)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Multiple concurrent requests often share overlapping prompt fragments (system prompts, few-shot examples, instruction templates) which leads to duplicated KV cache entries across requests and GPUs. This increases GPU memory pressure and reduces effective batch density. Current per-request KV stores deduplicate only at whole-prefix granularity and rely on CPU-side fingerprinting that is not aware of fragment reuse patterns.

Proposal: Build a GPU-resident fragment index + canonical fragment store that deduplicates prompt fragments at the sub-prefix level. The index maps a lightweight fingerprint (64-bit) -> canonical fragment pointer (GPU memory address + length + refcount metadata). When a request arrives, we segment the prompt into canonicalizable fragments (system prompt, instruction block, examples) and query the GPU index to reuse cached KV loops instead of duplicating entries. The design targets: (1) reduce peak GPU memory by ~15-40% on realistic PLG workloads, (2) improve continuous batching by increasing shared KV hits across batched requests, (3) keep lookup latency < 150us per fragment on A10/A100-class GPUs.

Scope: Implementation spans runtime KV layout changes, new GPU hash-index with open addressing, background compaction job for stale fragments, reference-counted eviction policy, and integration with request planner and batch coalescer.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical fragment store implemented and enabled behind flag --enable-fragment-store
End-to-end unit and integration tests for: fragment hashing, insertion, lookup, refcounting, eviction, and compaction
Benchmarks vs baseline showing >=15% reduction in peak KV memory for 75th-percentile workloads with many shared prompts
Lookup tail latency (99th) for fragment queries < 200us on supported GPU targets
No regression in token throughput (>98% of baseline) for synthetic benchmarks without shared fragments
Operational metrics: fragments_total, fragment_hits, fragment_misses, fragment_evictions, fragment_compactions exposed in console/tracing
Migration path for existing KV entries documented and tested (fall back to per-request store if flag off)

Runtime: implement GPU hash-index (robin-hood) and allocator hooks (Marco)
Planner: integrate fragment lookup into request canonicalization pipeline (Nora)
Eviction: implement LRU-like refcounted eviction and background compaction job (Marco)
Testing: microbench harness for fragment lookup latency and collision rate (QA)
Docs: internal design doc + upgrade notes for Dedicated/Private (Docs)
Telemetry: add metrics and dashboards in Console (Observability)
PRs: open incremental PRs for index, refcounting, and planner integration with feature flag gating
decisions: Use 64-bit fingerprint (XXH3-based) to balance collision probability and index memory overhead
Store canonical fragment metadata in GPU-resident structure; avoid CPU roundtrip for hot-path lookups
Choose open-addressing robin-hood hashing to keep probes bounded and cache-friendly on GPU
Reference counting is sufficient for correctness given our request lifecycle; soft-eviction will be used for low-refcount fragments
Background compaction will run on a low-priority CPU worker and schedule GPU defragmentation windows to avoid SLO impact
performance_targets: Reduce peak KV memory by >=15% on evaluated workloads
Fragment lookup p50 < 40us, p95 < 120us, p99 < 200us on A100
Collision rate < 1e-9 for production fingerprint set
Compaction window not to exceed 1% added CPU utilization under normal load
experiments: A/B run with fragment-store flag on 10% of traffic for 48h to validate memory savings and user-visible latency
Synthetic microbench with 10k distinct fragment corpus and varying reuse ratios (10%, 30%, 60%)
Stress test under continuous batching to measure impact on batch density and token throughput
dependencies: PM-417 (privacy review for shared canonicalization of customer prompts)
OBS-79 (add new fragment metrics to console)
risks: Fingerprint collisions could cause incorrect reuse — mitigated by verification-on-insert using short tag and fallbacks
GPU memory fragmentation from variable-length fragments — mitigated via periodic compaction and pooled allocators
Increased lookup latency harming tail latency SLOs — mitigated by microbench and feature-flagged rollout
Privacy/regulatory concerns if fragments include customer PII — mitigated by opt-out and redaction rules at ingestion
notes: Prototype (eng/prototypes/fragment-store) showed ~28% KV memory reduction on convo-heavy datasets (internal)
Found that breaking examples into individual shots increases reuse but raises lookup counts; trade-off controlled by segmentation heuristics
Plan to expose a per-customer fragment-policy (disable, allow, redact) for Dedicated/Private deployments
